issues.legal_issue: A plaint may be rejected as barred by law only when its statements, read as a whole and without resolving disputed facts, unambiguously establish the legal bar.
material_facts: The defendant applied to reject the plaint under Order VII Rule 11(d) on limitation grounds.
The plaint sought several forms of relief, including specific performance, damages, recovery or accounting for amounts collected, and injunctions.
Whether the amounts collected related to a period beyond the agreed lease term required evidence.
The trial court had rejected the application, but the High Court reversed that decision on the view that the claims centered on non-execution of the lease.
issues.conclusion: The High Court was wrong to hold that the plaint was barred on its face. The appeal was allowed, and the disputed limitation issues were left for the trial court to decide without any opinion on the merits.
issues.legal_principle: Under Order VII Rule 11(d) of the Code of Civil Procedure, the court examines the plaint’s averments, not the defendant’s pleas, and may reject the plaint only if those averments, read as a whole and without doubt or dispute, show that the suit is barred by law. Disputed questions cannot be decided at this stage. Order VI Rule 2(1) requires pleadings to state material facts, and the plaint cannot be dissected or read out of context. This approach is supported by Saleem Bhai v. State of Maharashtra, I.T.C. Ltd. v. Debts Recovery Appellate Tribunal, T. Arivandandam v. T.V. Satyapal, Roop Lal Sathi v. Nachhattar Singh Gill, Raptakos Brett & Co. Ltd. v. Ganesh Property, and Sopan Sukhdeo Sable v. Assistant Charity Commissioner. Limitation generally bars the remedy, not the underlying right; the Court referred in this connection to V. Subba Rao v. Secretary to Government, France B. Martins v. Mafalda Maria, and N. Balakrishnan v. M. Krishna Murthy.

predicates.application_to_reject_plaint: A party applies for rejection of a plaint on the ground that the suit is barred by law.
predicates.plaint_alone_unambiguously_shows_legal_b: The plaint, read as a whole and without resolving disputed facts or relying on material outside it, clearly establishes that the suit is barred by law.

issues.definition: When a party seeks rejection of a plaint and the plaint alone unambiguously shows a legal bar, the plaint must be rejected.

issues.legal_issue: A plaint containing independent claims cannot be rejected as time-barred when deciding whether the entire suit is barred requires resolving disputed facts.
material_facts: The plaint included claims concerning amounts allegedly collected by the defendant, as well as claims concerning execution of a lease and other relief.
The High Court treated non-execution of the lease as the focal point of all the claims.
The Supreme Court held that the other claims had independent existence and that determining the period to which the collections related required evidence.
The Supreme Court did not decide the merits of the claims or the limitation issues.
issues.conclusion: The plaint could not be rejected under Order VII Rule 11(d) on the basis that the entire suit was time-barred. The limitation issues were left for determination by the trial court in accordance with law.
issues.legal_principle: Order VII Rule 11(d) applies only where the plaint’s own statements show, without doubt or dispute, that the suit is barred. The whole plaint must be read together; claims must not be compartmentalized or reduced to a single asserted focal point when the plaint also advances independently existing claims. Disputed limitation questions requiring evidence are for later determination, not for decision on an application under that rule. The Court relied on Saleem Bhai v. State of Maharashtra, Raptakos Brett & Co. Ltd. v. Ganesh Property, and Sopan Sukhdeo Sable v. Assistant Charity Commissioner.

predicates.application_to_reject_plaint: A party applies for rejection of a plaint on the ground that the suit is barred by law.
predicates.plaint_contains_independent_claims: The plaint advances more than one claim, and at least one claim has an existence independent of the claim treated as the central claim.
predicates.limitation_depends_on_disputed_facts: Determining whether the claims are time-barred requires resolving disputed facts or receiving evidence.

issues.definition: When an application seeks rejection of a plaint that contains independent claims and limitation depends on disputed facts, the plaint is not rejected.
